readerTitle: Why the better tool often spreads slower
caseNote: 가상 사례 (인덕션 레인지 제조사 vs 식당용 재고 주문 앱, 프로젝트 관리 소프트웨어) + 실제 연구 (Ryan & Gross 1943 하이브리드 옥수수, Rogers의 확산 이론과 페루 물 끓이기 사례)
insight: 새 기술은 판매자에게서 구매자로 퍼지지 않고 사람에게서 사람으로 퍼진다. 확산 속도는 얼마나 더 좋은가보다 얼마나 쉽게 써 보고 남이 쓰는 걸 볼 수 있는가에 달려 있다.
misconception: 더 좋은 기술이면 고객이 알아서 바꾼다. 확산이 느리면 장점을 더 잘 설명하거나 가격을 내리면 된다.

sources.text: Ryan, B. & Gross, N. C. (1943). The diffusion of hybrid seed corn in two Iowa communities. Rural Sociology, 8(1), 15–24.
Rogers, E. M. (1962; 5th ed. 2003). Diffusion of Innovations. Free Press. (다섯 가지 특성, 페루 Los Molinas 물 끓이기 사례)
인덕션 레인지·재고 앱·프로젝트 관리 앱 사례와 차트 수치는 설명용 가상 예시

factChecks.note: Ryan & Gross(1943): 아이오와 두 지역 농민 대상, 하이브리드 옥수수 확산에 수년이 걸렸고 많은 농민이 처음에는 일부 밭에만 시험 재배했다는 점, 판매원이 최초 정보원으로 가장 흔했지만 이웃이 가장 큰 영향을 주었다는 결론을 원문으로 다시 확인하세요. 카드에는 구체적 연도·비율을 넣지 않았습니다.
Rogers의 다섯 가지 특성(상대적 이점, 호환성, 복잡성, 시험 가능성, 관찰 가능성)을 쉬운 말로 바꿔 적었습니다. 원래 용어와 의미가 맞는지 확인하세요.
페루 물 끓이기 사례: Rogers 책에 나오는 Los Molinas 마을의 2년 캠페인으로, 약 200가구 중 11가구만 채택했다고 알려져 있습니다. 카드에는 수치 없이 '일부만 설득'으로 적었습니다. 뜨거운 것/찬 것에 대한 지역 믿음과의 충돌이 원인이라는 설명을 확인하세요.
차트 수치는 모두 가상입니다(인덕션: 2,4,7,10,14,18%; 앱: 3,10,28,55,75,85%). S자 곡선 모양을 보여주기 위한 값입니다. 프로젝트 관리 앱의 8% 사용률도 가상입니다.

cards.title: Two better tools. One spread in months, one in years.
body: Two companies launched new tools for restaurants in the same city, in the same year. One made induction cooking ranges that cut energy bills and keep kitchens cooler. The other made a phone app for ordering stock from suppliers.
The range offered the bigger saving. Yet the app was in most kitchens years before the range.

image.label: A restaurant kitchen with a new range and a chef holding a phone
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 식당 주방 한쪽에 포장도 안 뜯은 새 인덕션 레인지가 덩그러니 서 있고, 반대쪽에서는 셰프 세 명이 각자 휴대폰으로 같은 앱 화면을 보며 웃고 있음. 실제 브랜드 로고 없음.

cards.title: You sell the induction range.
body: Chefs agree it's better on paper. After a year, only a few restaurants have bought one. You have budget for one big push.

options.text: Cut the price by 15% to make the decision easier
options.feedback: A lower price helps at the margin. But chefs aren't mainly stuck on price. They're stuck on the risk of switching a whole kitchen to a range they've never cooked on.

options.text: Print better brochures with detailed energy-savings data
options.feedback: More proof from the seller rarely moves cautious buyers. They trust what they see working in a kitchen like theirs more than what a supplier claims.

options.text: Install free units in three well-known kitchens and invite other chefs to cook on them
options.feedback: It costs more per kitchen, but it makes the range easy to try and easy to watch. You create the people others copy.

cards.title: Two very different curves
body: Share of the city's restaurants using each tool, by year. The app crawled at first, then shot up, then levelled off. Six years in, the range was still crawling.

image.label: Induction range crawls, ordering app S-curves
image.brief: Range 2% to 18% in 6 years vs app 3% to 85%.

cards.title: Diffusion and the S-curve
body: **Diffusion** is the way a new idea or tool spreads through a group of people. It rarely spreads at a steady pace.

Most people wait until someone like them has tried it and it worked. So adoption starts slowly, speeds up as each user persuades the next, then slows as few non-users are left. Plotted over time, it makes an S-shape: the **S-curve**.

image.label: An S-shaped adoption curve with people passing a tool along
image.brief: S자 곡선 인포그래픽. 곡선 아래쪽 평평한 구간에는 한두 사람만, 가파른 구간에는 사람들이 서로 도구를 건네주는 모습, 위쪽 평평한 구간에는 거의 모두가 사용. 구간 라벨 "Slow start", "Takes off", "Levels off".

cards.title: Iowa farmers trusted neighbors, not salesmen.
body: In 1943, sociologists Bryce Ryan and Neal Gross studied how hybrid seed corn spread among farmers in two Iowa communities. The seed gave clearly higher yields, yet most farmers took years to switch.

Many first planted it on a small part of their land. Salesmen were often how farmers first heard of it, but neighbors' results were what convinced them. The study helped inspire Everett Rogers' 1962 book *Diffusion of Innovations*.

image.label: A farm field with a small test strip of different corn
image.brief: 따뜻한 일러스트. 넓은 옥수수밭 한 귀퉁이에만 키가 더 큰 옥수수 시험 구획이 있고, 울타리 너머 이웃 농부가 그것을 유심히 바라봄. 1940년대 분위기, 상표나 로고 없음.

cards.title: What makes something spread fast
body: Rogers named five traits that speed adoption. The app had more of them than the range.
list: **Clear advantage:** obviously better than the old way
**Fits current habits:** little change to how people already work
**Easy to try:** you can test it small before committing
**Easy to see:** others can watch it working
cards.callout: The app was free to try and chefs saw it on each other's phones. The range needed new wiring and a risky week of relearning.

cards.title: Better doesn't guarantee the curve.
body: The S-curve is easy to draw afterwards. While you're in the slow start, a slow start and a stall look the same.

Rogers described a two-year campaign in a Peruvian village to get families to boil drinking water. It persuaded only a small share, partly because boiling clashed with local beliefs about hot and cold. A real benefit lost to poor fit with habits.
Pushing harder rarely fixes that. Changing the product, or who tries it first, often does.

cards.title: Now it's a software feature.
body: You run a project-management app for small teams. Six months ago you launched time tracking. Teams that use it love it, but only 8% of customers have turned it on.

options.text: Email every customer explaining the benefits
options.feedback: Cheap and fast, but it's the seller talking again. Expect a small bump, not a curve.

options.text: Let any team try it on one project in one click, and show which teammates already use it
options.feedback: Trying becomes small and safe, and use becomes visible to peers. That's what steepens the curve.

options.text: Add more time-tracking features to widen the advantage
options.feedback: The advantage is already real for those who use it. More features add complexity, which slows adoption further.

cards.title: New things spread when people can try them and see them work.
body: Adoption moves from person to person, not from brochure to buyer. Being better gets you in the game. Being easy to try and easy to watch sets the speed.
**Try it today:** pick one new thing you want customers or staff to adopt. Write down how someone could try it in under an hour, and who they'd see using it first.
